stick_information_theory_the_measure_of_.question: Information theory - the measure of a message, verified and sealed

ticks.claim: [the bit] A fair coin has Shannon entropy H = -sum p log2 p = 1.000 bit (sealed through information_theory.INFO_VERIFY) - the unit of information, the answer to one yes/no question. This is the logarithm on the solve path, measuring a choice.
[distance in code] The Hamming distance between 10110 and 11010 is 2 - two positions differ (sealed); the number of single-bit errors that separate two codewords, the basis of error-correction.
[a clean channel] A binary symmetric channel with error rate 0 has capacity C = 1 - H2(0) = 1 bit per use (sealed) - Shannon's limit, the most a channel can carry.
[the ground] Shannon's 1948 axioms: information is -sum p log p, and a channel has a hard capacity no code can beat. Sealed where applied; the theory is the floor the whole digital world stands on.
[declined] The MEANING or value of a message is not information in this sense - the engine measures the message's surprise and the channel's limit, not what the message is worth.
